purpose: Verify AP payment idempotency and void history, eligibility and debt rechecks, atomic allocation and currency boundaries, a shared-invoice race, permissions and amount precision, payment-method evidence, and a consistent detail snapshot.
data: Seven cases on one shared HTTP/MySQL application, three synthetic identities, eight suppliers and twelve invoices. The large-amount assertion uses two invoice rows to verify decimal aggregation.
concurrency: Serial cases and existing workers. One two-request race for the same invoice and one controlled reader/writer interleaving.
thresholds: All seven functional cases pass. Existing global 92/83/90 and 39 per-file coverage floors remain in place.
trigger: Existing ci.yml functional server MySQL shards, discovery, workers and trigger scope. Same jobs and scheduler.
cost: Local case durations sum to 1.045 seconds (UTC) and 1.074 seconds (Asia/Hong_Kong), excluding suite startup overhead. CI impact has not been measured.

cases: AP records payment against an archived supplier, replays commands, and retains void history
AP rechecks debt and supplier eligibility when creating and confirming a payment
AP allocation is atomic across invoices and later spends prepayments by supplier and currency
two payments competing for the same open invoice cannot allocate it twice
AP payment permissions, currency precision and aging totals above a single document limit
AP requires method evidence for new payments and blocks legacy drafts from taking a number without it
AP payment detail keeps one read snapshot across a concurrent allocation commit
